input.prompt:
Paint a production 2D game inventory atlas for 灵葫大作战. Exactly six original matched spirit-wing pairs, centered in a regular 3-column by 2-row grid on a 1536 by 1024 image. SIX 512 by 512 invisible cells, row-major centers exactly at (256,256), (768,256), (1280,256), (256,768), (768,768), (1280,768). In each cell, the entire left-and-right pair together is no more than 380px wide and 330px high and has at least 66px clear empty margin to all cell edges. All air must be genuine zero-alpha transparency, including each specified interior opening. Nothing outside the six pairs. No tile, panel, lettering, numbers, marks, canvas texture, ground shadow, oval shadow, cast shadow, sparkles, floating particles or loose secondary object. Only the six isolated wing pair icons.

Three references are supplied. First is QQTang source morphology for mapping the item positions and broad silhouettes. Use only the broad visual identity, opening/connection and proportions described below; ignore its oval floor shadows, texture, palette, labels and gray board. The next two are the game's canonical style, not objects to trace. These six are wholly new Daoist Q-style wardrobe icons with thick crisp contours, rounded sculpted materials, simple large color regions, low-to-medium detail, jade / porcelain / bronze / silk, rounded bevel accents, warm upper-left key lighting. They should be readable at 32px on pale parchment and deep jade. Each cell shows one full bilateral symmetrical pair facing flat forward in catalogue view, no person or attachment context. Keep distinct materials and shapes.

Top left, 25 LAN-SILK BUTTERFLY. One centrally joined butterfly with four rounded panels, bold tall oval upper lobes and short scalloped lower lobes, spring-gold woven silk, jade orchid-green tip sections and cinnabar lower wing tips, dark ink-bronze piping, short golden central fitting and no dangly element. Top middle, 26 INK BAT. Two separate outward-curving broad scalloped bat wings, a true narrow transparent vertical opening between their inner tips. Black plum-indigo lacquer membranes, vivid cinnabar red edge panels, two short upward outer spikes and thick clear bat silhouette; bronze beads only attached at the inward tips. Top right, 27 PORCELAIN CRANE. Two separate ivory-white and lilac porcelain feather wings with each inner root curled like a ruyi cloud and a true transparent center gap. Each half is short and broad, with three individually rounded down-fanning feather lobes and small blue-gray tips; warm narrow antique-gold rim for visibility. No halo or ornament in the center.
Bottom left, 111 ROSE BLOSSOM. Two separate broad rose-pink silk-petal wings with a true slim transparent opening in the middle; on each half a boldly visible layered crimson round rose near the inward root and two broad soft pink pointed petal panels opening outward, dark crimson edge. Bottom middle, 133 JADE CICADA. Two separate beautiful long slender pointed teal-jade upper wing blades tilted up and outward, with one small rounded violet-and-teal lobed wing below per side, oversized readable silhouette, a few large filigree veins integrated into solid stone, and a clearly open transparent center. No butterfly roundness. Bottom right, 147 EMBER PHOENIX. A single joined upward-opening U-shaped pair, a narrow bronze-gold curl clasp connects the very bottom center while an ample transparent U-shaped opening remains above it. Overlapping flame-shaped carved vermilion-orange feathers, gold highlights and ember red tips, swept up and outward; no crest above the center opening and no phoenix head.

Final image is only the six production icons in the strict cell positions, high contrast and visually distinct, native transparent background.
